evidence.text: Declared annual income is roughly $38,000; deposits in this window total ~$85,000.
Nine separate cash deposits, each between $9,200 and $9,800 — all just under the $10,000 CTR threshold.
Deposits were split across three different branches in the same city on overlapping days.
Teller notes record the customer asking at what dollar amount deposits 'get reported'.

evidence.text: Twelve cash deposits over 11 days, every one between $8,800 and $9,600, none reaching $10,000.
Historical average is ~$14,000/month in deposits; this window is ~$112,000.
Deposits made at ATMs and two branches, spread to avoid any single $10k+ event.
No corresponding increase in card sales, invoices, or payroll to explain the cash surge.

alert.amount: 7 cash deposits $9,000-$9,700, then a $60k outbound wire
alert.note: sub-threshold cash followed by lump-sum wire

evidence.text: Seven cash deposits, each $9,000-$9,700, made over six days.
Two days after the last deposit, a single $60,000 wire left the account to an unrelated third party.
The wire beneficiary has no prior relationship or transaction history with the customer.
Customer's declared income (~$45k/yr) is far below the ~$66k moved in this window.
Six cash deposits in three days, each $9,400-$9,900, totaling ~$57,000.
Customer recently sold a car privately; a bill of sale for $9,500 is on file.
The remaining ~$47,500 in deposits has no documented source.
Deposits were deliberately kept under $10,000 despite the customer holding a single account.
Wire beneficiary 'Tavriya Metals' screens as an exact match to a current OFAC SDN-list entity.
Payment reference cites shipment routing through a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction.
Customer onboarding is only one year old with limited transaction history.
The invoice supporting the wire lists goods (industrial metals) consistent with the beneficiary's stated trade.
Wire originator is a bank branch located in a comprehensively sanctioned country.
Originating entity name matches a designated party on the SDN list (strong match).
Stated purpose is 'consulting services' but no contract or invoice is on file.
Customer's prior inbound wires were all domestic and under $10,000.
Bill of lading names a vessel that appears on a sanctions-linked vessel watchlist.
Shipping route transits a port in a sanctioned jurisdiction not disclosed on the payment order.
Counterparty itself does not match any sanctions list.
Customer has a long clean history of legitimate freight payments.

evidence.text: Customer is flagged as a close family member of a foreign head of state (PEP by association).
A $480,000 inbound wire is immediately followed by payment to a luxury art dealer.
Source-of-wealth documentation on file does not account for the wire's origin.
Enhanced due diligence required for this customer tier was never completed.
Customer is a senior government procurement official (confirmed PEP).
The $260,000 wire originates from a private contractor that bids on the customer's agency's tenders.
Payment reference is a vague 'advisory fee' with no supporting agreement.
Timing coincides with a large public contract award by the customer's agency.
$340,000 arrived via five inbound wires and $332,000 left via seven outbound wires within nine days.
Closing balance returned to near zero; the account functions as a pass-through.
Inbound and outbound counterparties are all unrelated third parties in different jurisdictions.
The company has no employees, website, or evidence of actual advisory services.
Fourteen unrelated individuals sent small P2P transfers totaling $88,000 in two weeks.
The aggregated funds were forwarded to three overseas accounts almost immediately.
A student account with no employment income received and forwarded ~$85,000 net.
The customer stated a friend asked to 'use the account to receive some payments'.
Funds moved in a loop across four accounts the customer controls, ending near the origin.
Each hop added a different invoice reference with no underlying goods or services.
The pattern obscures the original source of the $500,000.
Registered in a secrecy jurisdiction with a nominee director.

customer.name: Sunrise Bakery Inc
customer.profile: established retail bakery, avg monthly cash ~$40k

evidence.text: Single cash deposit of $11,500 following a holiday weekend.
POS/register totals reconcile exactly with the deposit amount.
Cash deposits of this size are routine for this business and consistent with 9 years of history.
A CTR is auto-filed for the over-$10k cash event; no other red flags present.
The $130,000 wire is labeled 'home sale proceeds' and matches a recorded property closing.
A signed settlement statement from the title company is on file for the same amount and date.
Funds remained in the account and were partly moved to the customer's own brokerage.
No sanctions, PEP, or structuring indicators are present.
Deposits rise every spring and fall each year, matching the landscaping season.
This year's amounts and cadence are in line with the prior three seasons on record.
Invoices and a customer job schedule support the volume of work.
Deposit sizes vary naturally ($6k-$9k) with no evidence of deliberate threshold avoidance.
A fixed $4,500 transfer goes to the same beneficiary on the 1st of each month.
The beneficiary is an assisted-living facility; a signed care agreement is on file.
The pattern has been stable and unchanged for over two years.
No connection to any sanctioned party or high-risk jurisdiction.
The $210,000 inbound wire originates from a well-known SBA lender.
A fully executed equipment-financing loan agreement is on file for the same amount.
Funds were used to pay a dental-equipment vendor within a week.
No sanctions, PEP, structuring, or layering indicators are present.
A single $18,000 cash deposit corresponds to a documented vehicle sale.
A signed bill of sale and buyer ID copy are attached to the transaction.
Deposit was made openly as one transaction, not split to avoid reporting.
A CTR is required and filed for the over-$10k cash; no suspicion indicators otherwise.
Daily cash deposits of $10,000-$15,000 match a cash-heavy grocery's normal takings.
Deposits reconcile to register Z-reports each day.
CTRs are filed for the over-$10k events as required.
Amounts are openly over the threshold — the opposite of structuring.

alert.note: many small inbound from different senders

evidence.text: Inbound transfers of $2,000-$5,000 arrive from different individuals each month.
Each corresponds to an issued invoice for a wedding or event shoot.
Client names and amounts match the customer's booking calendar and invoices.
Funds are spent on ordinary living and business expenses, not forwarded onward.
Three cash deposits over ten days, each between $8,500 and $9,400.
Customer's income is genuinely variable and has occasionally reached these levels before.
No source documentation is on file, but none was ever requested for this tier.
Only three deposits — not clearly a deliberate pattern, but not clearly benign either.
The originator name is a partial/weak match to a sanctions-list entity but with a different country and address.
The match score is below the bank's auto-escalation threshold and may be a false positive.
Supporting invoice looks legitimate but has not yet been verified with the shipper.
No secondary red flags (amount and purpose are consistent with the business).
A $40,000 wire arrived from an overseas account in the customer's own name at another bank.
Stated purpose is 'relocation savings transfer', which is plausible for a new arrival.
Account is only two months old, so there is no behavioral baseline to compare against.
No sanctions or PEP hits, but source-of-funds evidence has not been provided yet.
Two cash deposits of $9,700 in the same week.
Customer says these are monthly rent payments from two tenants who pay in cash.
Lease agreements exist but the stated rents ($9,700 each) are unusually high and unverified.
Pattern could be legitimate rent collection or could be sub-threshold structuring.
The end-user address on the shipping docs is in a sanctioned jurisdiction, though the invoiced buyer is in a neutral country.
Goods are export-controlled dual-use components subject to sanctions rules.
The buyer entity itself does not appear on any sanctions list.
The routing appears structured to disguise the true destination of the goods.
